Tanabe entry says dawn of eighth day; report offers following-dawn interpretation for agreement. Literal January 27 dawn precedes nominal earthquake in Japan-time conversion, so that reading conflicts with the proposed causal sequence.

Tanabe/Shinjō heights derive from alternative assumptions about building/field elevations, tide, flow depth and later land movement. The 5.4 m storehouse scenario requires an uncertain site identification; it is not a directly measured 1700 watermark.
Survivor responses include disturbed, apparently undisturbed and unclassified trees; killed-cedar dating uses an Ozette reference chronology.

Two complete related root-radius series and one terminal decade transcribed (642 widths); seven GF2RTC transcription mistakes corrected transparently. Within-root correlations computed; external calendar crossdating not reproduced.

cases.next_test: Obtain raw ring widths and rerun crossdating; inspect calendar reference tables and original snowstorm entries supporting the Tsugaruishi month correction; reproduce tsunami travel-time inference with arrival uncertainty. Inspect Tanabe preceding entry and parallel Mandaiki passage; seek independent day-boundary translation. cases.title: Coyote Canyon mammoth and reworked camel comparison
cases.category: fossil context and flood sediment chronology
cases.place: Coyote Canyon, Benton County, Washington, USA

claims.statement: Seven sediment OSL ages are reported at two sigma; the nearby camel bone is reported older than host flood sediment, while the mammoth humerus age is compatible with part of the sequence.

Bone plan combines several excavation levels; section contacts include uncertain projections and overlying paleosol/loess. Authors acknowledge that slope wash can produce repeat beds within waning flood stages.
Three measurements from one camel metatarsal precede the reported combined age; original laboratory certificates remain uninspected.
Documents the weighted-mean and chi-square method used for the conditional local pooling check, not an execution of the authors model.
Preliminary abstract reports gnawing on ten of eleven ribs; specimen IDs and raw mark measurements are absent.
Authors relate bone spread and nearby bed thickness to repeated burial and cite the gnawing report; this is dependent interpretation, not independent replication.
Preliminary XRF abstract distinguishes major units; it does not provide raw data or independently validate the flood-event count.

cases.physical_evidence: Published excavation figures 4-7 and sample tables 2-4 visually inspected; seven OSL rows checked. No field or specimen inspection.
cases.surviving_documents: 2021 original study and its citations to earlier bone dating.
cases.source_interpretation: Repeated flood deposition; possible flood-related mammoth death; reworking of the older camel bone.
cases.investigation_inference: Death, transport and sediment burial must be tested separately. Five flood OSL intervals overlap at 18.32-19.05 ka, so these ranges alone do not resolve event multiplicity. Conditional independent one-sigma pooling of three camel assays gives Q=8.66093 (df=2, p=0.01316); precise combined age needs laboratory/model audit.
competing_explanations: Mammoth death associated with a flood and later burial
Death before transport or deposition
Older camel bone reworked into younger sediment
Dating or context errors requiring laboratory and field checks
cases.counterevidence: Older camel bone challenges equating all fossils in a flood deposit with the flood age. Broad OSL overlap prevents claiming that central-age differences alone prove separate events.
cases.next_test: Recover original mammoth assays and camel laboratory/model records; link identified gnawed ribs to beds and mark/sediment overprints to test exposure timing.
